identification: Australian fire brigade cast iron fire alarm box (street/building call box), arched-top door, red paint. Door cast 'BREAK THE GLASS PRESS THE BUTTON' around a round window (glass gone, button plate rusty), a script monogram below, then 'FIRE ALARM'; 'FIRE' painted on the side. Inside: complete alarm transmitter with toothed code wheel (painted dial), clockwork, relay coils, terminal block, bell, and a bakelite telephone handset on a hook, i.e. the 'fire alarm telephone' type used by Australian brigades (probably c1930s-1950s). Monogram is very worn: most likely 'NSWFB' (New South Wales Fire Brigades) in the same script style as the NSWFB box sold on eBay, but could be MFB; not certain. About 40-45 cm high judging by photos (not given).

viewing_check: Read the monogram in good light (NSWFB vs MFB vs other); look for a maker's plate on the mechanism (e.g. STC, Siemens, Gamewell, Ericsson) and a box number; check the code wheel turns and the clockwork is not seized; check the door hinges and lock (key present?), cracks in the casting, and whether the handset cord is intact; weigh it for postage.
